newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-HOLDER SAMPRAS TUMBLES OUT OF PARIS OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HOLDER SAMPRAS TUMBLES OUT OF PARIS OPEN.

text.p: Defending champion Pete Sampras went out at his first hurdle in the Paris Open, a 6-4 6-4 second round loser to Marc Rosset of Switzerland on Wednesday.

"He's six foot seven (2.01 metres) and it feels like he's slam-dunking on you all the time," Sampras said, using a basketball term to describe the thundering service of the lanky Swiss, who sent down 20 aces in the 75-minute match.
Sampras, who lost Sunday's Stuttgart Open final to Boris Becker, said: "The key to the match was whenever I had a break point he came up with an ace."
Sampras looked like he would manage to break Rosset when the Swiss was 5-4 up in the second set, and stay in the match.
But Rosset came up with aces as answers to successive break points and only failed to clinch the set and match sooner because he double faulted twice in the game.
Sampras had no complaints about the Parisian crowd which sixth seed Becker said made a constant and unsettling noise during his upset 6-3 5-7 6-4 defeat by Carlos Moya of Spain.
